text:
jenna: heads up — noticed an odd p99 jump in the merged latency dashboard after yesterday's canary :grimacing:. per-endpoint panes look normal, but the combined line spikes. anyone seen this?

matt: saw a blip, thought it was retries. which merged view are you looking at? the 'all endpoints' rollup?

jenna: yep — Console > Latency > All endpoints (last 24h). p50/p95 look steady, p99 jumps ~18:22 UTC. endpoints individually (by prefix) show flat lines.

kevin: did we change routing weights or fallback policy in that canary? fallback to beefier model can skew tail if samples merge oddly.

ash: quick dump of sample origins around spike:
```
origin=client count=8421
origin=server count=120
origin=cache_hit count=47
origin=fallback count=6
```
counts look small for the cache/fallback, but merge could amplify.

sam: also check transport vs server time — sometimes gateway queueing shows up in merged p99 if we mix http and gRPC?

deploy-bot: Canary deployment r-2026.03.17-2 finished at 2026-03-17T18:17:12Z to 10% traffic.

luke: FYI our merged percentile calc uses tdigest rollups from different backends. tdigest merging isn't associative for tiny shards and can create artificial tail bumps when one shard has low samples.

matt: ahhh that rings a bell. endpoint panes use local percentiles computed per-shard then displayed; merged uses rollup of tdigest objects across shards. mismatch possible.

kevin: the routing policy tweak I pushed bumped fallback weight from 0 -> 0.02 for canary. small absolute traffic but skewed latency distribution (fallback model is slower). with tdigest merge that could produce a p99 bump even if per-endpoint slices hide it.

jenna: so two contributors: fallback slower, and tdigest merge artifact. how do we make this less alarming to users?

luke: short fix: annotate merged charts with a sample-count heatmap and add a tooltip "percentile provenance: tdigest-merged". long fix: compute percentiles from raw sample sketch at query time when sample counts are low.

ash: I'll open a tiny dashboard patch to show sample_count under the p99 trace. simple change in query: add sum(sample_count) grouped by timeslice.

maria: UX suggestion: when rollout/route weights changed in past 2h show a banner on the latency pane like "rollout in progress: percentiles may be inconsistent across rollups" and point to docs. less surprise for customers.

kevin: Agree. Also we should treat fallback-tagged requests as a separate cohort by default in the merged view until sample size > N.

sam: also add a note to the internal runbook: "If merged p99 jumps but endpoints look fine, check (1) sample_provenance, (2) rollback/fallback weights, (3) tdigest shard sample counts."

jenna: thx. action items?

ash: PR coming for sample_count strip in chart (https://github.com/redwood/console/pull/XXXX).

luke: I'll draft the tdigest-provenance tooltip copy and open an ops issue for query-time percentile fallback.

maria: I'll add the rollout banner copy and a short docs blurb.

kevin: I'll revert the fallback weight for canary to 0.005 for next hour to keep noise down, then re-evaluate with A/B.

jenna: awesome. let's regroup after fixes and watch the next canary window. thanks all :rocket:
